```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
```

## Load the weather data 

```{r}
library(p8105.datasets)
data("weather_df")
```

## Remember this plot..? 

```{r}
weather_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax)) + 
  geom_point(aes(color = name), alpha = .5)
```

## Labels

```{r}
weather_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax)) + 
  geom_point(aes(color = name), alpha = .5) +
  labs(
    title = "Temperature plot",
    x = "Minimum daily temperature (C)",
    y = "Maximum daily temperature (C)", 
    color = "Location",
    caption = "Data from the rnoaa package; temperatures in 2017."
  )
```


## Scales

Start with the same plot; x and y scales

X axis scale
```{r}
weather_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax)) + 
  geom_point(aes(color = name), alpha = .5) +
  labs(
    title = "Temperature plot",
    x = "Minimum daily temperature (C)",
    y = "Maximum daily temperature (C)", 
    color = "Location",
    caption = "Data from the rnoaa package; temperatures in 2017."
  ) + 
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(-15, 0, 15),
    labels = c("-15 ºC", "0", "15")
  )
```

Adding y axis scale

```{r}
weather_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax)) + 
  geom_point(aes(color = name), alpha = .5) +
  labs(
    title = "Temperature plot",
    x = "Minimum daily temperature (C)",
    y = "Maximum daily temperature (C)", 
    color = "Location",
    caption = "Data from the rnoaa package; temperatures in 2017."
  ) + 
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(-15, 0, 15),
    labels = c("-15 ºC", "0", "15"), 
    limits = c(-20, 30)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    trans = "sqrt", 
    position = "right"
  )
```


Look at colour scales 

```{r}
weather_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax)) + 
  geom_point(aes(color = name), alpha = .5) +
  labs(
    title = "Temperature plot",
    x = "Minimum daily temperature (C)",
    y = "Maximum daily temperature (C)", 
    caption = "Data from the rnoaa package; temperatures in 2017."
  ) +
  scale_color_hue(
    name = "Location",  
    h = c(100, 300))
```

Viridis package: 

```{r}
ggp_temp_plot = 
weather_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax)) + 
  geom_point(aes(color = name), alpha = .5) +
  labs(
    title = "Temperature plot",
    x = "Minimum daily temperature (C)",
    y = "Maximum daily temperature (C)", 
    caption = "Data from the rnoaa package; temperatures in 2017."
  ) +
 viridis:: scale_color_viridis(
   name = "Location",
   discrete = TRUE)
```


## Themes

Themes are used to modify non-data elements of a plot (ie. controls things like background color and location of the the legend)

Shift the legend 

```{r}
weather_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax)) + 
  geom_point(aes(color = name), alpha = .5) +
  labs(
    title = "Temperature plot",
    x = "Minimum daily temperature (C)",
    y = "Maximum daily temperature (C)", 
    caption = "Data from the rnoaa package; temperatures in 2017."
  ) +
 viridis:: scale_color_viridis(
   name = "Location",
   discrete = TRUE) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Change the overall theme 

```{r}
weather_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax)) + 
  geom_point(aes(color = name), alpha = .5) +
  labs(
    title = "Temperature plot",
    x = "Minimum daily temperature (C)",
    y = "Maximum daily temperature (C)", 
    caption = "Data from the rnoaa package; temperatures in 2017."
  ) +
 viridis:: scale_color_viridis(
   name = "Location",
   discrete = TRUE) +
  theme_minimal() + 
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```


```{r}
ggp_temp_plot +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```


```{r}
ggp_temp_plot +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r}
ggp_temp_plot +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```


## Setting options 

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(tidyverse)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  fig.width = 6, 
  fig.asp = .6,
  out.width = "90%"
)

theme_set(theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "bottom"))

options(
  ggplot2.continuous.colour = "viridis",
  ggplot2.continuous.fill = "viridis"
)

scale_colour_discrete = scale_colour_viridis_d
scale_fill_discrete = scale_fill_viridis_d
```


## Data args in `geom`

```{r}
central_park_df = 
  weather_df |> 
  filter(name == "CentralPark_NY")

molokai_df = 
  weather_df |> 
  filter(name == "Molokai_HI")

ggplot(data = molokai_df, aes(x = date, y = tmax, color = name)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line(data = central_park_df)
```

## `patchwork`

Remember faceting? 

```{r}
weather_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, fill = name)) + 
  geom_density(alpha = .5) +
facet_grid(. ~ name)
```

What happens when you want multipanel plots but can't facet?

```{r}
tmax_tmin_p = 
  weather_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax, color = name)) +
  geom_point(alpha = .5) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

prcp_dens_p = 
  weather_df |> 
  filter(prcp > 0) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = prcp, fill = name)) +
  geom_density(alpha = .5)
  theme(legend.position = "none")

tmax_date_p = 
  weather_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = date, y = tmax, color = name)) +
  geom_point(alpha = .5) + 
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE) + 
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

tmax_tmin_p + prcp_dens_p

tmax_tmin_p + prcp_dens_p + tmax_date_p

tmax_tmin_p + (prcp_dens_p + tmax_date_p)
(tmax_tmin_p + prcp_dens_p) / tmax_date_p
```


## Data manipulation 

```{r}
weather_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = name, y = tmax, fill = name)) + 
  geom_violin(alpha = .5)
```

Control your factors.
If you want to change the order (reorder categorical predictor on X axis)

Option 1; just include Molokai_HI (makes this first), keeps rest in same order
```{r}
weather_df |> 
  mutate(
    name = factor(name),
    name = forcats::fct_relevel(name, c("Molokai_HI"))
  ) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = name, y = tmax, fill = name)) + 
  geom_violin(alpha = .5)
```

Option 2; specify exact order you want 

```{r}
weather_df |> 
  mutate(
    name = factor(name),
    name = forcats::fct_relevel(name, c("Molokai_HI", "CentralPark_NY", "Waterhole_WA"))
  ) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = name, y = tmax)) + 
  geom_violin(aes(fill = name), color = "blue", alpha = .5) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Option 3; reorders name according to tmax values in each name (place)
-sorts from lowest to highest tmax (based on each place's median temp value)
```{r}
weather_df |> 
  mutate(name = forcats::fct_reorder(name, tmax)) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = name, y = tmax)) +
  geom_violin(aes(fill = name), colour = "blue", alpha = .5) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```



What if I wanted densities for tmin and tmax simultaneously? 

shows tmax and tmin values for central park NY 
```{r}
weather_df |> 
  filter(name == "CentralPark_NY") |> 
  pivot_longer(
    tmax:tmin,
    names_to = "observation", 
    values_to = "temp") |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = temp, fill = observation)) +
  geom_density(alpha = .5) 
```

Makes density plots with tmin and tmax for each place (one panel per place)
```{r}
weather_df |> 
  pivot_longer(
    tmax:tmin,
    names_to = "observation", 
    values_to = "temp") |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = temp, fill = observation)) +
  geom_density(alpha = .5) +
  facet_grid(. ~ name) 
```

Makes density plots with tmin and tmax for each place (one panel per place), with viridis colour scheme
```{r}
weather_df |> 
  select(name, tmax, tmin) |> 
  pivot_longer(
    tmax:tmin,
    names_to = "observation", 
    values_to = "temp") |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = temp, fill = observation)) +
  geom_density(alpha = .5) +
  facet_grid(. ~ name) +
  viridis::scale_fill_viridis(discrete = TRUE)
```
